concerns.text: FR-001 requires a task that creates `data/raw/github-code-sample.csv` via streaming download, but T018 is left unchecked (marked as pending) leaving the core data‑download requirement uncovered.
FR-006 mandates evaluation on the real HumanEval dataset; T070 (and related tasks T031, T072) are still incomplete and reference synthetic‑data fallback, violating the no‑fallback clause.
FR-007 specifies segment‑level (`function body`) correlation, yet tasks T033/T032a join on `problem_id`, creating a mismatch that weakens the required segment‑level analysis.
FR-009 requires PII scanning of all files; T017 cannot run because the raw dataset file is missing (see FR-001 issue), breaking the Constitution Principle III data‑hygiene guarantee.
FR-010 demands checksums for all output files; T025 (and analogous T036, T044) are marked incomplete, so no checksum is recorded for generated CSVs.
SC-001 (24‑hour processing limit) has no completed performance‑validation task; T024 remains unresolved, leaving the success criterion unverified.
SC-002 (memory‑usage ≤ 7 GB) lacks any monitoring or validation task; T023 is missing, so the memory budget cannot be demonstrated.
SC-003 (≥ 1000 processed segments) is marked completed but depends on an unresolved claim, providing no concrete evidence that the segment count threshold is met.
SC-004 (statistically significant correlation) is not satisfied because correlation tasks T032, T033, T034 are incomplete and no `correlation_results.csv` is produced.
SC-005 (hyper‑parameter documentation) is only partially addressed; T074 (verification of hyperparameters location) is pending, so the documentation requirement remains unproven.
SC-007 (PII absence verification) references T052 but it is not linked to actual scan results from T017, leaving the PII‑absence guarantee unvalidated.
Retroactive narrowing: T018c uses a tiny (~5‑file) sample for US‑1 dependency, which weakens FR-001’s requirement for a 500 MB corpus and violates the specification’s full‑scale data requirement.
